findings.summary: Module imports the eager `env` singleton and constructs a Pool at top-level; any code path that needs only `createDb` or `Db` type pays the env validation + TCP setup cost on import.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the top-level `const pool = new Pool(...)` and `export const db = createDb(pool)` lines. Keep only the `createDb(pool)` factory and type exports. Have main.ts (or buildApp) build the Pool from a loadEnv() result and call createDb(pool) once, then pass `db` through DI. This is the same fail-fast DI seam pattern flagged in wave-3 F-001 (env.ts) and is required for the wave-7 buildApp({ env }) override.

findings.summary: Pool sizing constants (max, idleTimeoutMillis, connectionTimeoutMillis) are hardcoded; task description specified "sized from env" but env schema does not declare DB_POOL_MAX or related vars.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend apps/api/src/shared/env.ts with DB_POOL_MAX / DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS (Zod coerce.number with sensible defaults) and read them inside createDb's caller, or update the task spec to drop the env-sizing requirement. The current literal `max: 10` will be wrong under the docker-compose api-migrate + api + seed concurrent boot per ARCHITECTURE §4.3.

findings.summary: DATABASE_URL fallback `?? ''` silently masks an unset env var; drizzle-kit will then fail with an opaque pg connection error rather than a clear "env missing" message.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? ''` with an explicit assertion: `const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL; if (!url) throw new Error('DATABASE_URL is required for drizzle-kit'); ... dbCredentials: { url }`. drizzle-kit runs at migration time only — it is fine to fail loud here without going through loadEnv (which would pull the whole API env schema into a CLI config).

findings.summary: `const _env = loadEnv(); void _env;` pattern is opaque; future readers may delete the apparently-unused binding and break the fail-fast import-time check.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a single statement and a comment: `// Fail-fast on missing/short JWT_SECRET (enriched bullet 10). Result intentionally discarded — secret is passed per-call.` followed by `loadEnv();`. Or wrap in a named helper `assertEnvLoadable()` exported from shared/env.ts so the intent is captured at the call site.

findings.summary: `throw new Error('JWT payload shape invalid')` uses a bare Error instead of the project's AppError hierarchy; ARCHITECTURE §5.2 mandates UnauthorizedError (401) for invalid credentials so errorHandler maps it correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Import { UnauthorizedError } from '../../shared/errors.js' and throw `new UnauthorizedError('Invalid session token')` instead. Same applies to whatever wraps the jwtVerify call site (authn middleware in wave-5) — but at this layer the AppError mapping is appropriate.

findings.summary: Schema barrel already re-exports ../modules/auth/schema.js; task spec said "initially empty — downstream tasks add the imports". Forward-looking re-export only works because wave-5's auth/schema.ts is already on disk.
findings.suggested_fix: Acceptable in the re-entry context (file authored ahead-of-wave by earlier orchestrator run). No action needed; flagging as scope drift signal so the wave-5 reviewer does not double-add this re-export when auth/schema.ts is re-verified.
